title: Cross-team Celebration Remarks — Scratch
content:
Notes to self: this is a loose, conversational set of remarks for the upcoming all-hands where we want to pause and celebrate recent cross-team wins. Keep it short (3–4 minutes), human, and specific. Avoid exec-speak; use concrete examples and one or two funny/relatable micro-stories.

Theme: "We shipped reliably together" — emphasis on coordination, small teams making outsized impact, and operational improvements that matter to customers.

Opening (15–20s):
- Quick hello: "Hi everyone — I want to take a couple minutes to highlight a few wins and people who made them possible."
- Set the ask: "No slides, just a few real thank-yous and one quick story."

Top 3 points (45–60s total):
1) Customer reliability win: dedicated capacity handoff for BigRetail pilot happened last week — zero downtime during the rollout. Shout-outs to infra (Ravi), SRE (Marta), and the solutions team (Jordan) for the late-night runbook sync.
   - Quick stat: 99.98% availability during the rollout window, average p95 latency improved by ~8%.
2) Cost/perf optimization: Optimize team + Serving Runtime pilot reduced per-token cost for the most common seq length by ~22% in beta. Leads: Priyanka + Andres.
   - Small anecdote: Andres found a kernel fallback that saved ~0.5ms/token on long tails — nerdy but directly translatable to $$ saved.
3) Developer experience: SDK v2 internal beta reached 50 teams and fixed a major onboarding friction that used to take 3 emails and a half-day debug. Shout-outs to DevEx (Ethan, Mikaela).

Micro-story (30–45s):
- Quick human moment: during the BigRetail rollover, an unexpected region quota hiccup looked like it might stall things. Someone (Riley) DM'd the oncall, who then paged an infra engineer, who then texted the PM, and we rotated a tiny capacity pool for 12 minutes — teamwork kept customers happy. Mention this to highlight practical cross-team coordination, not heroic lone-wolf saves.

Shout-outs (30s): call out specific people and why:
- Ravi (infra) — for the handoff coordination and a clear runbook update.
- Priyanka (Optimize) — for the profiling work and clear before/after numbers.
- Ethan (DevEx) — for shepherding SDK rollout and the new onboarding guide.
- Riley (oncall) — for fast escalation and calm communications.
- Solutions + Customer Success (unnamed group shout) — for being pragmatic with the pilot and giving timely feedback.

Anticipated Qs / Quick answers (prep, 1–2 lines each):
- Q: Are we pausing other projects to support pilots? A: No — these were prioritized within existing roadmaps; where extra effort was needed, teams coordinated short shifts rather than long-term reassignments.
- Q: Any customer credit/penalty? A: Not for this event — the pilot contract included a clear handoff and we executed within those bounds.
- Q: Will these improvements be available to self-serve customers? A: Early versions are targeted for Dedicated customers first; some SDK/Optimize changes will roll to hosted tiers after validation.

Tone checklist (for me to remember):
- Short, grateful, concrete.
- No jargon. "Latency" is okay if tied to what it means for customers.
- Avoid numbers-heavy deep dives — save that for follow-up email or product blog.
- Use first names, not just teams.

Logistics / delivery notes:
- No slides, but have 2 short lines prepared on the main slide deck in case they want text.
- Mic cue: after CEO set-up, I jump in. Keep watch for the 4-minute mark.
- After remarks: propose a 24-hour shout-out thread in #all-hands-shoutouts and follow up with an email summarizing the wins + links to docs.

Follow-up items (post-all-hands):
- Draft shout-out Slack thread: assign to Jonas.
- Short internal blog post with metrics + brief engineering notes — ask Priyanka for 2-paragraph blurb.
- Make sure runbook changes from rollout are checked in and link the PR in follow-up email (Ravi).

Open items / things I still need to confirm before live: 
- Exact p95 latency delta number from telemetry (waiting on SLO dashboard snapshot, ask observability).
- Confirmation that BigRetail is okay with public mention (PM to confirm).
- Final list of names for shout-outs (I will trim to 4–6).

Draft closing line options (pick one):
- "That’s it — big thanks, everyone. Let’s keep making this stuff boring in the best way possible."
- "Thanks to everyone who leaned in — your work shows up as reliability and predictability for customers, and that’s the point."
- "Short and simple: excellent work. Now back to shipping."

Random notes to self (do not say on stage):
- Remember to breathe. Smile. Pause after each name to let applause land.
- Bring the anecdote, not the slide. People remember small human moments.

End of scratchpad. Use this to craft final 3‑minute script and pass to Jonas for copy-edit and to Aisha for timing run.
